sec: Typhoid pathogenesis and treatment; dengue incubation, course and symptoms

items.q: Pathogenesis of typhoid — match — 1) Entry 2) Multiplication 3) Seeding 4) Re-entry … A) Liver, spleen and bone marrow B) Via the bloodstream C) Gallbladder, biliary system and lymphatic system of bowel D) Intestinal tract with ileocaecal hyperplasia
items.exp: 'Via blood stream (m/c) → In liver, spleen & bone marrow multiply, re-enter → Invades & multiplies in Gallbladder, Biliary system, Lymphatic system of bowel → Pass into intestinal tract and causes ileocoecal hyperplasia'. (Book p1055)

items.q: Which route does the page print as the most common for dissemination in typhoid?
Judge the pathogenesis: I The organism multiplies in liver, spleen and bone marrow. II The gallbladder and biliary system are seeded and the organism later re-enters the bowel.
items.exp: Both statements follow the printed chain through the gallbladder, biliary system and bowel lymphatics. (Book p1055)

items.q: Which anatomical site is printed as the site of the lesion produced after intestinal re-entry?
items.exp: 'Pass into intestinal tract and causes ileocaecal hyperplasia'. (Book p1055)

items.q: Treatment — match — 1) Uncomplicated 2) Complicated … A) Ceftriaxone 2 g IV for 14 days B) Co-trimoxazole double strength BD for 14 days, or azithromycin 1 g once daily for 7 days
items.exp: 'Uncomplicated cases : Cotrimoxazole (DS) BD × 14 days OR Azithromycin 1g OD × 7 days'; 'Complicated cases : Ceftriaxone 2g I/V × 14 days'. (Book p1055)

items.q: Duration printed for azithromycin in uncomplicated enteric fever?
Duration printed for intravenous ceftriaxone in complicated enteric fever?
Dengue disease course — match — 1) Day 1 to 3 2) Day 4 onwards … A) NS1 antigen negative, fever subsides, rash appears B) NS1 antigen positive
items.exp: 'Day 1 to 3 : NS-1 antigen positive'; 'Day 4 onwards : NS-1 antigen negative; Fever subsides; Rash'. (Book p1055)

items.q: Dengue symptoms — match — 1) Fever 2) Pain 3) Gut … A) High grade B) Vomiting C) Headache and retro-orbital pain
items.exp: 'Symptoms : High grade fever, Headache, · Retro-orbital pain, · vomiting'. (Book p1055)

items.q: What does the page print about the platelet count in dengue without warning signs?
opts: It falls but is given as not below 50,000
items.exp: 'Day 4 onwards : ↓ Platelet counts (Not < 50,000)' with '· Leucopenia' and 'Dengue without warning signs'. (Book p1055)

items.q: Which white-cell change is printed on day 4 onwards in dengue?
Judge the dengue block: I NS1 antigen is positive from day 1 to day 3 and negative from day 4. II The fever subsides and the rash appears from day 4 onwards.
items.exp: 'Day 1 to 3 : NS-1 antigen positive'; 'Day 4 onwards : NS-1 antigen negative', 'Fever subsides', 'Rash'. (Book p1055)
